purpose: Declare which social platforms this network posts to (see platforms, which is the switch), how a paused platform behaves (see pause_mode), and prevent long-term starvation of smaller brands on the enabled ones while preserving daily caps.

platforms._read_me_first: This block is the on/off switch for each social platform. Nothing else in the repository decides whether a platform posts. To turn one on or off, change its "enabled" value here and commit. That is the entire change. A platform switched OFF must also record who paused it, when and why, plus a "pause_mode" saying what happens to its content meanwhile: "dormant" means nothing is produced at all (LinkedIn), and "draft_by_hand" means the API lane is off but the day's posts are still written to reports/social-drafts.md to be posted by hand (X). pause_mode is ignored while enabled is true, so re-enabling a platform stays a one-boolean change either way.

x.HOW_TO_TURN_X_BACK_ON: Change "enabled" on the next line from false to true, and commit. That is the whole switch, exactly as it is for LinkedIn. The X entries already sitting in data/social-queue.json start going out again on their own -- they were never deleted, never re-labelled and carry no per-row pause mark, so nothing has to be rebuilt or un-marked. "pause_mode" below is inert the moment enabled is true; leave it as it is. X's API is pay-per-use and a post carrying a URL costs about $0.20, so turning this on means funding the developer account first -- until then every write answers HTTP 402 credits-depleted. While it is off, distribution does NOT stop: see pause_mode.
x.paused_reason: owner_decision_2026-08-29: "im not funding X so find a $0 workaround or kill it." X's API is pay-per-use with no free tier -- every write this repository has ever made answered HTTP 402 problems/credits-depleted, starting with the very first request, and nothing has ever posted. At roughly $0.20 per post with a URL, eight a day is about $48/month. The owner has decided not to pay it. This is NOT a dormant pause: X is off for API POSTING only, and distribution continues by hand -- every scheduled run still writes the day's eight highest-value posts to reports/social-drafts.md, and she copies them out and marks the batch done in data/social-draft-ledger.json. That is what pause_mode "draft_by_hand" means and why it is not "dormant" like LinkedIn.

delivery_route._read_me_first: A delivery route is another way for an X post to LEAVE. It is not a second platform and it does not change what is posted: the same queue, the same priority order, the same brand rotation, the same text. X's own API stays off and is contacted zero times -- it is pay-per-use at about $0.20 per post carrying a URL, and every post here carries one. Buffer publishes to the same X profile from its free plan at no per-post cost, so while this route is on, the day's X posts go into Buffer's queue instead of onto reports/social-drafts.md to be pasted by hand. Turn it off by setting "enabled" below to false: the hand-post sheet comes back on the next run, unchanged, with nothing to undo.
delivery_route.credential: BUFFER_ACCESS_TOKEN (repository secret; never in this file)
delivery_route.channel: Discovered at runtime: the first channel on the Buffer account whose service is "twitter" (Buffer's schema has no "x" service). Not pinned here, so reconnecting the channel in Buffer does not require a commit.
delivery_route.daily_limit: Discovered at runtime from Buffer's own dailyPostingLimits query and used as a hard ceiling, then capped again by daily_limit above. Never hardcoded: a number typed here stays wrong after Buffer changes it, and being wrong about a ceiling is what produced 581 requests in 76 seconds on 2026-08-29.
delivery_route.queued_is_not_published: Buffer ACCEPTING a post is not X publishing it. An accepted entry is stamped status "buffer_queued" with its Buffer post id, and Buffer sends it at the channel's next posting slot. Nothing in this repository reports it as posted.
delivery_route.STATUS_2026_08_29: Wired, authorized and unable to run until one thing happens in Buffer: the account (seq.taylor@gmail.com, organization "My Organization") has ONE channel connected and it is TikTok. No X channel exists, so there is nothing to post to. The plan allows 3 channels and 1 is used. Connect the X profile at buffer.com -> Channels -> New Channel, and this route starts carrying the day's posts on the very next scheduled run with no commit, no secret and no code change. Until then every run says so in reports/social-publisher-report.json under delivery_routes.x.why_not_used, and the posts keep going out by hand exactly as they do today.

linkedin.HOW_TO_TURN_LINKEDIN_BACK_ON: Change "enabled" on the next line from false to true, and commit. That is the whole switch. The 581 LinkedIn posts already sitting in data/social-queue.json start going out again on their own -- they were never deleted, never re-labelled, and nothing has to be rebuilt or un-marked. Two repository secrets also have to exist for a post to actually send: LINKEDIN_ACCESS_TOKEN and LINKEDIN_AUTHOR_URN. If you flip this on before adding them, nothing breaks: each run says "linkedin_on_but_uncredentialled" in reports/social-publisher-report.json and nothing else changes. (X is no longer posting either -- it is paused for posting with pause_mode "draft_by_hand", so its content goes out by hand from reports/social-drafts.md.)
linkedin.paused_reason: owner_decision_2026-08-29: "drop linkedin for now its not important", and "i might bring linkedin back at anytime". LinkedIn is paused on purpose and is expected to come back. It is NOT off because LINKEDIN_ACCESS_TOKEN / LINKEDIN_AUTHOR_URN are missing from repository secrets -- that absence follows from this decision rather than causing it. This record exists so "paused by choice", "on but uncredentialled" and "on and posting" are three visibly different states instead of one blank secret.

rotation.rule: Sort by prior posted count divided by quota weight, then rotate the brand start position by date ordinal.
rotation.guarantee: No brand is permanently locked behind earlier queue order when eligible posts exist.

dream-wedding-builder.rule: Four domains do not create four separate social allocations.
